technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Cloud Stream binder abstractions to support pluggable binder types (Rabbit, Redis, Kafka) for module channels.
Leverage Spring Boot's externalized configuration mechanisms (e.g., application.properties/yml, command-line arguments) to pass overrides via external config files.
Integrate the official Cloud Foundry Java Client to refactor the Cloud Controller (CC) Service Provider Interface (SPI) deployer for improved design and performance.
Use Maven profiles or a similar dependency management strategy to allow users to select their preferred Hadoop distribution and load the appropriate libraries into the classpath.
Align dependency upgrades (Spring Integration 4.2, Spring 4.2.1, AMQP 1.5) with the existing build system to ensure compatibility across the framework.
assumptions: The developer is highly experienced with the Spring Framework, Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d), Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s), and Spring XD.
The existing codebase is modular and accessible, allowing for straightforward extraction and migration of modules.
Unit and integration testing are included as part of the development activities for each user story.
The 'XD' refers to Spring XD, and 's-c-s' refers to Spring Cloud Stream.
No new infrastructure setup is required; existing CI/CD pipelines and repositories will be used.

activities.activity_description: Extract the Kafka module from the XD repository and migrate it to the s-c-s repository, adapting it to function as a sink for building streaming pipelines.
Extract the Rabbit module from the XD repository and migrate it to the s-c-s repository, adapting it to function as a sink for building streaming pipelines.
Add support for having different binder types for module channels, allowing Rabbit, Redis, or Kafka to be plugged in as the source or sink to read and write respectively.
Add the capability to pass any overrides via an external config file to influence and override default module configurations (e.g., module resolution from a different Maven coordinate).
Refactor the Cloud Controller Service Provider Interface (SPI) deployer using the Cloud Foundry Java Client to improve overall design and performance.
Add an option to choose the Hadoop distribution of choice so that the right Hadoop libraries can be loaded into the classpath.
Move the header-enricher module from the modules repository to the XD proper codebase.
Upgrade project dependencies to Spring Integration 4.2, Spring 4.2.1, and AMQP 1.5 to take advantage of the latest improvements.
Perform comprehensive end-to-end testing and validation of all migrated modules, new binder support, external configurations, and dependency upgrades.
